title: ROC curve as a named Se–Sp display
dek: Wikipedia ROC: TPR vs FPR as a threshold moves. AUC is a concordance summary, not a likelihood and not a PPV.
story: A ROC curve on Wikipedia plots sensitivity against 1−specificity as you slide a threshold on a score. AUC is the probability a random diseased case scores above a random non-case (plus ties handling).
stats-se-sp and stats-predictive-values own the point-threshold world and prevalence. This card is the encyclopedia curve so AUC is not reported as 'accuracy' or as PPV.
Class imbalance does not change AUC's concordance meaning, but it does change whether AUC is the decision-relevant number (calibration, PPV, utility do).
deep: Youden's J picks a threshold by Se+Sp−1, ignoring prevalence and costs.
Precision–recall curves are the imbalanced-data neighbour.
AUC comparisons need a variance (DeLong or bootstrap), not two naked numbers.
A well-separated ROC can still be poorly calibrated.

visual.caption: Score in, threshold slides, Se and 1−Sp trace the curve. PPV still needs prevalence — a different plate.
